column1: # Game profile of The Rogue Prince of Persia (Switch, update 1.1.0 = v262144). Plays on the Mac
# Evil Empire's game on Unity 6000.0.64f1 IL2CPP with FMOD, SDK 20.5.29, NVN. The NSP script's provisional profile, unchanged in its keys: no rewriter cut, no host change of its own

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# every module main imports from (subsdk0 = the SDK's movie library)
# the NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory) and main never sets a heap: a 5 GB block with a 4.375 GB alias region, where the game maps its memory itself
# (up to 1.77 GB mapped from the title through the first level)
# every shader is under Data/ (41,629) or in main (11); the .nrr and Plugins groups find none but stay, as shader_* keys are in every shader's cache key

column1: # 60 fps (30 on the Switch), up to 120 on the Mac: the game sets Unity's QualitySettings.vSyncCount to 2, which Unity hands to NVN as present interval 2, and steps by the time that
# really passed. The rewriter finds vSyncCount and Application.targetFrameRate through Unity's internal-call table in any build it reads (dm/tools/unity_fps.py), the host writes the
# target there (hle_fpslock.c) and presents at it. 120 needs the display's vsync event at 120 too (hle_nvn.c nvn_vsync_hz): Unity's NVN device waits for each vblank.
# The speed checked at 30, 60 (a timed walk) and 120 (the user's play test)
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0: the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
